children: Anthropic Details Massive Claude Distillation
Distillation involves using responses from a more capable AI model to help train another system.
In a report released Thursday, Anthropic said the activity it identified went beyond ordinary model use and involved unauthorized, large-scale extraction of Claude’s capabilities.

Alibaba allegedly generated more than 151 million exchanges with Claude between May and July, making it the largest distillation campaign Anthropic said it had detected. The activity reportedly peaked at nearly 3 million exchanges per day across more than 3,500 fraudulent accounts.
Anthropic said Alibaba used Claude outputs to help train its
Qwen
models and also relied on the model for areas including reinforcement learning and model architecture research.
Moonshot, DeepSeek Also Accused
Anthropic said Moonshot AI, the company behind
Kimi
, routed some customer requests to Claude without users’ knowledge.
During one 10-day period, nearly 300,000 requests were allegedly relayed to Anthropic, while more than 23 million exchanges were attributed to Moonshot between May and July.
The company also accused DeepSeek of similar activity, saying it observed more than 12 million distillation attacks over 14 days in July.
Anthropic said some of the intercepted requests contained sensitive information and raised concerns about privacy and terms-of-service violations.
The report covered activity across multiple areas, including cyber operations, surveillance, scams, biological misuse, weapons development and AI model distillation.
Alibaba, Moonshot, DeepSeek and Xiaomi did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comment.
